newsitem.title: UK: Stg's strength threatens 100,000 UK jobs - economist.
newsitem.headline: Stg's strength threatens 100,000 UK jobs - economist.

text.p: The strength of the pound threatens the loss of 100,000 manufacturing jobs in Britain over the next year, a leading economist said.

Andrew Sentance, director of the London Business School's Centre for Economic Forecasting, said the pound -- up nearly 25 percent on a trade-weighted basis in less than a year -- would knock about two percent of manufacturing output over the next year.

But the good news is that strong domestic demand, improving export markets, healthy profit margins and structural changes to British industry in recent years all mean the impact of a sky-high pound would be less traumatic than in the 1980s, when it forced a 10 percent drop in capacity.

More good news is that Sentance does not expect sterling to retain its strength beyond this year. "The evidence that a strong pound is having an impact on trade flows and growth prospects is likely to lead to a weaker trend in sterling next year," he said.
"As the UK economy slows down and prospects in continental Europe improve, interest rate prospects are likely to become less supportive of the pound."
British base rates stand at 6.75 percent, after three increases in as many months, while German rates are skulking at just 2.5 percent.
Sentance forecast the pound would be worth 2.6 marks by the end of 1997, compared with more than three now.
Nonetheless, he urged the Bank of England to be cautious about pushing interest rates up too sharply. Its last quarter-point rise came just last week.

"The Bank was right to limit its recent increase to a quarter of one percentage point, and a rise in interest rates to around seven percent later this year should be sufficient to create an orderly slowdown in the economy next year," he said.
"Going far beyond this would run the danger of overkill, adding unnecessarily to the slowdown next year."
